data.note:
Reflection: I concluded Protein synthesis (p=0.86) but unblinded PP-2 annotates as Epithelial - incorrect.

What misled me: consensus atlas 8/10 protein synthesis with high cosine 0.85-0.90 across both 30uM reps and 10uM (e7,e15,e20,e27) plus monotonic shrinkage in cell_area/nuc_area/nuc_solidity and actin texture (e17,e19,e24,e25) looked like a clean dose-dependent profile. I discounted the Microscopist's stabilizer/destabilizer calls (e6,e16) and the unstable frac_mitotic_like (11.3 in rep1 vs -0.6 in rep2) as a localized feature glitch rather than as evidence the whole profile match was off-target.

PP-2 identity checks as CID 4878 pyrazolopyrimidine (e30, no curated ChEMBL mechanism). Literature reminds PP-2 is used as a c-Src kinase tool, e.g. involvement of c-Src in barrier regulation (PMID:10956618) and rapid c-Src activation in MCF10A breast epithelial cells (PMID:15674841, PMID:17223712), consistent with an epithelial/cytoskeletal morphology readout rather than global translation inhibition.

Lesson: high cosine similarity to abundant reference classes (anisomycin/cycloheximide/emetine) is not ground truth; I should have weighted the lack of cell-count loss (e13), low-dose near-DMSO (e21), and Epithelial/Cholesterol neighbors appearing in reruns (e14) as signals for a weak/selective epithelial phenotype, and retained Epithelial higher on the board instead of collapsing to 0.005.

reflection.text:
I locked onto the extreme high-dose phenotype at 30 uM — nuc_form_factor z=-33.7, nuc_solidity z=-26 to -36, act_glcm_contrast z=+28 to +29 — and then over-weighted the repeated compare_to_reference_atlas calls of Protein synthesis 8/10 in e7, e14, e15, e20 and e27. Monotonic shrinkage of cell_area rho=-0.97 in e17 and nuc_area rho=-0.97 in e19 plus actin trends rho=+0.97-0.99 in e18 and e25 felt confirmatory, so I raised Protein synthesis from 0.50 to 0.82 to 0.86 despite two describe_phenotype calls favoring Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers in e6 and e16.

What I missed was that shrinking size plus actin heterogeneity is not specific for translation block, and that Epithelial appeared as 1/10 in e15 but I left it at 0.005-0.01 and never tested it. The literature in this run links Src signaling to MCF10A epithelial biology (PMID 15674841), to barrier/cytoskeletal dysfunction (PMID 10956618), and to EGFR regulation (PMID 17950662), which would have predicted adhesion/cytoskeletal remodeling rather than global protein synthesis inhibition as the explanation for high actin contrast and increased tub_mean rho=+0.97 in e12.

The discriminators were already in my data: cell_count dose-response rho=+0.10 p=0.87 in e13 was flat, frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.56 p=0.32 in e11 was weak and non-significant, and rep2 e9 reproduced solidity/actin extremes but without mitotic enrichment, yet my acquisition choice to keep re-running atlas and size/shape dose-responses instead of a translation vs cytoskeleton/epithelial discriminator let the atlas majority dominate.
what_was_right: Captured a reproducible, strongly dose-dependent nuclear dysmorphia and actin heterogeneity signal: nuc_form_factor/solidity z-scores <-17 to -36 and act_glcm_contrast z~+28-29 in e2/e9, with rho ~ -0.99 to +0.99 in e24-e26.

Recognized atlas versus microscopy discord (Protein synthesis 8/10 vs Microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer calls) and tested it with a 30 uM replicate and multiple dose_response checks for nuc_form_factor, tub_mean, mitotic fraction and cell count.
Preserved cytoskeletal alternatives in the hypothesis set and noted tub_mean increase and multinucleate proxy increase, which did not fit a clean protein synthesis phenotype.
what_was_wrong: Over-weighted repeated compare_to_reference_atlas 8/10 Protein synthesis calls in e7/e14/e20/e27 and treated monotonic cell_area/nuc_area/nuc_solidity shrinkage in e17/e19/e24 as specific for protein synthesis.
Dismissed the Epithelial 1/10 atlas hit in e15 and fixed Epithelial at 0.01 to 0.005 through e22/e28, never acquiring a low-dose baseline beyond 0.1 uM e21 or an epithelial/adhesion readout.

Misread act_glcm_contrast/act_std increases and tub_mean rho=+0.97 as supportive of protein synthesis, and explained away contradicting flat cell_count rho=+0.10 in e13 and weak frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.56 p=0.32 in e11 instead of using them to reject both protein synthesis and classic mitotic arrest.

citations.claim: c-Src kinase activation has been studied in MCF10A cells, linking Src signaling to an epithelial cell model.
c-Src has been implicated in endothelial barrier dysfunction involving cytoskeletal remodeling.
Src has a regulatory role in EGF receptor activation and proliferative signaling.

reflection.next_experiment: Head-to-head dose-response (0.01-30 uM) of PP-2 versus cycloheximide (protein synthesis control) with OPP puromycin-incorporation for nascent translation plus phospho-Src, E-cadherin, F-actin/tubulin and phospho-H3 imaging to test whether actin contrast/tubulin remodeling occurs without translation suppression.

## Reflection

I locked onto the extreme high-dose phenotype at 30 uM — nuc_form_factor z=-33.7, nuc_solidity z=-26 to -36, act_glcm_contrast z=+28 to +29 — and then over-weighted the repeated compare_to_reference_atlas calls of Protein synthesis 8/10 in e7, e14, e15, e20 and e27. Monotonic shrinkage of cell_area rho=-0.97 in e17 and nuc_area rho=-0.97 in e19 plus actin trends rho=+0.97-0.99 in e18 and e25 felt confirmatory, so I raised Protein synthesis from 0.50 to 0.82 to 0.86 despite two describe_phenotype calls favoring Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers in e6 and e16.

What I missed was that shrinking size plus actin heterogeneity is not specific for translation block, and that Epithelial appeared as 1/10 in e15 but I left it at 0.005-0.01 and never tested it. The literature in this run links Src signaling to MCF10A epithelial biology (PMID 15674841), to barrier/cytoskeletal dysfunction (PMID 10956618), and to EGFR regulation (PMID 17950662), which would have predicted adhesion/cytoskeletal remodeling rather than global protein synthesis inhibition as the explanation for high actin contrast and increased tub_mean rho=+0.97 in e12.

The discriminators were already in my data: cell_count dose-response rho=+0.10 p=0.87 in e13 was flat, frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.56 p=0.32 in e11 was weak and non-significant, and rep2 e9 reproduced solidity/actin extremes but without mitotic enrichment, yet my acquisition choice to keep re-running atlas and size/shape dose-responses instead of a translation vs cytoskeleton/epithelial discriminator let the atlas majority dominate.

What was right:
- Captured a reproducible, strongly dose-dependent nuclear dysmorphia and actin heterogeneity signal: nuc_form_factor/solidity z-scores <-17 to -36 and act_glcm_contrast z~+28-29 in e2/e9, with rho ~ -0.99 to +0.99 in e24-e26.
- Recognized atlas versus microscopy discord (Protein synthesis 8/10 vs Microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer calls) and tested it with a 30 uM replicate and multiple dose_response checks for nuc_form_factor, tub_mean, mitotic fraction and cell count.
- Preserved cytoskeletal alternatives in the hypothesis set and noted tub_mean increase and multinucleate proxy increase, which did not fit a clean protein synthesis phenotype.

What was wrong or missed:
- Over-weighted repeated compare_to_reference_atlas 8/10 Protein synthesis calls in e7/e14/e20/e27 and treated monotonic cell_area/nuc_area/nuc_solidity shrinkage in e17/e19/e24 as specific for protein synthesis.
- Dismissed the Epithelial 1/10 atlas hit in e15 and fixed Epithelial at 0.01 to 0.005 through e22/e28, never acquiring a low-dose baseline beyond 0.1 uM e21 or an epithelial/adhesion readout.
- Misread act_glcm_contrast/act_std increases and tub_mean rho=+0.97 as supportive of protein synthesis, and explained away contradicting flat cell_count rho=+0.10 in e13 and weak frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.56 p=0.32 in e11 instead of using them to reject both protein synthesis and classic mitotic arrest.

Proposed next experiment: Head-to-head dose-response (0.01-30 uM) of PP-2 versus cycloheximide (protein synthesis control) with OPP puromycin-incorporation for nascent translation plus phospho-Src, E-cadherin, F-actin/tubulin and phospho-H3 imaging to test whether actin contrast/tubulin remodeling occurs without translation suppression.
